rounds.proof_sketch: With block_size=256, there are 8 warps. Original: warp 0 computes sum of warp_sums[0..7]. Mutant: warps 1-7 each compute sum of warp_sums[0..7]. Both compute identical values because all warps read the same shared memory and perform identical shuffle reductions. Racing writes all write the same value.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes which warps execute the final cross-warp reduction, but not the computed result. In the original, warp 0 reduces warp_sums[0..7]. In the mutant, each of warps 1-7 independently reduces the same warp_sums[0..7] values using identical shuffle operations, obtaining the same total. The racing writes to warp_sums[0] are all writing the same correct sum, making the race benign. After __syncthreads(), all threads read the same correct value from warp_sums[0] in both versions.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed configuration. The cross-warp reduction is symmetric - any warp(s) computing the sum of the 8 warp partial sums will produce the identical result. The mutation only changes which warp(s) do this work, not the output.
rounds.recommendations: When designing warp-level reductions, consider adding assertions or thread-id-dependent magic values to distinguish which warp performed a computation. Alternatively, mutation testing tools could be enhanced to recognize symmetric reduction patterns as mutation-equivalent contexts.
